3	## Conventions
4	
5	- **Story ID** `S-n`. **Acceptance criterion ID** `AC-n.m`, where n is the story number.
6	- Each story names its **role** (`app-roles.md`) and the **job** it serves (`jobs-to-be-done.md`).
7	- **Scope**: `v1` means we are building it now. `Backlog` means it is recorded for later and will not be built.
8	- **Status** reflects what the running app does *today*. Every story starts as `Not implemented`. A story moves to `Implemented` only when **all** of its acceptance criteria pass in automated tests **and** in a manual check by the human reviewer. If any criterion is not met, the story stays `Not implemented`, and a note says which criterion fails.
9	- Every acceptance criterion is covered by at least one automated test whose title starts with its ID, for example `[AC-2.4] ...`.
10	- Exact on-screen text (labels, messages) is defined in `spec/technical-spec.md` §7 (copy deck). Messages quoted below must match it character for character.
11	- Unless stated otherwise, examples assume the currency is **PKR**. Amounts in the summary are shown as `Rs 1,234.56`. In the schedule, the currency symbol appears only in the column headers.

55	## S-1 Calculate the monthly payment
56	**Role:** R-1 Prospective Borrower · **Serves:** J-1 · **Scope:** v1 · **Status:** Not implemented
57	
58	"As a Prospective Borrower, I want to enter a loan amount, interest rate and tenure and get the monthly payment, so that I can check whether it fits my budget."
59	
60	- **AC-1.1** Given an empty form, when I enter loan amount `1000000`, rate `12`, tenure `1` with unit **Years** and Calculate, then **Monthly payment** shows `Rs 88,848.79`.
61	- **AC-1.2** Given an empty form, when I enter `1000000`, `12`, tenure `12` with unit **Months** and Calculate, then **Monthly payment** shows `Rs 88,848.79` (the same as 1 year).
62	- **AC-1.3** Given L-B entered as `2500000`, `18`, `5` **Years**, when I Calculate, then **Monthly payment** shows `Rs 63,483.57`.
63	- **AC-1.4** Given a zero rate (L-C: `120000`, `0`, `12` **Months**), when I Calculate, then **Monthly payment** shows `Rs 10,000.00`.
64	- **AC-1.5** Given a one-month loan (L-D: `100000`, `10`, `1` **Months**), when I Calculate, then **Monthly payment** shows `Rs 100,833.33`.
65	- **AC-1.6** Given the smallest accepted values (L-MIN: `1000`, `0.01`, `1` **Months**), when I Calculate, then **Monthly payment** shows `Rs 1,000.01`.
66	- **AC-1.7** Given the largest accepted values (L-MAX: `1000000000`, `50`, `40` **Years**), when I Calculate, then **Monthly payment** shows `Rs 41,666,666.80`.
67	- **AC-1.8** Given the loan amount is typed with thousands separators, as `1,000,000` or in lakh style as `10,00,000`, when I Calculate with `12` and `1` **Years**, then the result is the same as AC-1.1.
68	- **AC-1.9** Given values with leading or trailing spaces (`␣1000000␣`, `␣12␣`, `␣1␣`), when I Calculate, then the spaces are ignored and the result is the same as AC-1.1.
69	- **AC-1.10** Given the rate is typed with a trailing percent sign (`12%`), when I Calculate with `1000000` and `1` **Years**, then the result is the same as AC-1.1.
70	- **AC-1.11** Given I have just calculated L-A, when I Calculate again without changing anything, then the same results are shown again.
71	- **AC-1.12** Given a first visit, when the page loads, then the tenure unit is **Years**, all three inputs are empty, and no results are shown.

73	## S-2 Clear messages for invalid input
74	**Role:** R-1 Prospective Borrower · **Serves:** J-1 · **Scope:** v1 · **Status:** Not implemented
75	
76	"As a Prospective Borrower, I want to be told clearly what is wrong with what I typed, so that I can fix it and never act on a figure built from bad input."
77	
78	Error messages appear directly below the field they refer to. While any error is shown, no results are shown.
79	
80	- **AC-2.1** Given an empty form, when I Calculate, then I see `Enter a loan amount.`, `Enter an interest rate.` and `Enter a loan tenure.` under the matching fields, no results are shown, and focus moves to **Loan amount**.
81	- **AC-2.2** Given loan amount `abc` (rate `12`, tenure `1` **Years**), when I Calculate, then I see `Loan amount must be a number.` and no results.
82	- **AC-2.3** Given loan amount `1e6`, when I Calculate, then I see `Loan amount must be a number.` (scientific notation is not accepted).
83	- **AC-2.4** Given loan amount `0`, `-500` or `999.99` (each tried separately), when I Calculate, then I see `Loan amount must be between 1,000 and 1,000,000,000.`
84	- **AC-2.5** Given loan amount `1000000000.01`, when I Calculate, then I see `Loan amount must be between 1,000 and 1,000,000,000.`; and given loan amount `1000000000`, no loan-amount message is shown.
85	- **AC-2.6** Given loan amount `1000.555`, when I Calculate, then I see `Loan amount can have at most 2 decimal places.`
86	- **AC-2.7** Given rate `-1` or `50.01`, when I Calculate, then I see `Interest rate must be between 0 and 50%.`; and given rate `0` or `50`, no rate message is shown.
87	- **AC-2.8** Given rate `twelve`, when I Calculate, then I see `Interest rate must be a number.`; and given rate `12.345`, I see `Interest rate can have at most 2 decimal places.`
88	- **AC-2.9** Given tenure `2.5` with unit **Years**, when I Calculate, then I see `Loan tenure must be a whole number.`
89	- **AC-2.10** Given unit **Years** and tenure `0` or `41`, when I Calculate, then I see `Loan tenure must be between 1 and 40 years.`; given unit **Months** and tenure `0` or `481`, I see `Loan tenure must be between 1 and 480 months.`; and tenure `40` **Years** or `480` **Months** shows no tenure message.
90	- **AC-2.11** Given an invalid loan amount and an invalid rate with a valid tenure, when I Calculate, then both messages are shown at the same time and focus moves to **Loan amount** (the first invalid field).
91	- **AC-2.12** Given results for L-A are showing, when I change the loan amount to `abc` and Calculate, then the previous results and schedule are removed and only the error message is shown.
92	- **AC-2.13** Given a message is showing under **Loan amount** and another under **Annual interest rate**, when I type in the **Loan amount** field, then the loan-amount message disappears and the rate message stays until the next Calculate.
93	- **AC-2.14** Given any error is showing, when I correct the input to L-A values and Calculate, then the L-A results are shown and no error messages remain.
94	- **AC-2.15** Given a loan amount of 40 nines (`9999999999999999999999999999999999999999`), when I Calculate, then I see `Loan amount must be between 1,000 and 1,000,000,000.` and the page stays responsive.
95	- **AC-2.16** Given any invalid input in this story, when I Calculate, then the page never shows a blank screen or a browser error, and no uncaught error is raised in the browser console.

97	## S-3 See total interest and total amount payable
98	**Role:** R-1 Prospective Borrower · **Serves:** J-2 · **Scope:** v1 · **Status:** Not implemented
99	
100	"As a Prospective Borrower, I want to see the total interest and the total I will repay, so that I can compare the true cost of different offers."
101	
102	- **AC-3.1** Given L-A, when I Calculate, then **Total interest** shows `Rs 66,185.45` and **Total amount payable** shows `Rs 1,066,185.45`.
103	- **AC-3.2** Given L-B, when I Calculate, then **Total interest** shows `Rs 1,309,014.14` and **Total amount payable** shows `Rs 3,809,014.14`.
104	- **AC-3.3** Given L-C (0%), when I Calculate, then **Total interest** shows `Rs 0.00` and **Total amount payable** shows `Rs 120,000.00`.
105	- **AC-3.4** Given L-MIN, when I Calculate, then **Total interest** shows `Rs 0.01` and **Total amount payable** shows `Rs 1,000.01`.
106	- **AC-3.5** Given L-MAX, when I Calculate, then **Total interest** shows `Rs 19,000,000,061.79` and **Total amount payable** shows `Rs 20,000,000,061.79`, in full, with no truncation, ellipsis or scientific notation.

109	## S-4 Results always match the inputs on screen
110	**Role:** R-1 Prospective Borrower · **Serves:** J-1 · **Scope:** v1 · **Status:** Not implemented
111	
112	"As a Prospective Borrower, I want results to disappear as soon as I change an input, so that I never mistake old figures for the loan I am now looking at."
113	
114	- **AC-4.1** Given results for L-A are showing, when I change the loan amount, the rate or the tenure value, then the results summary and the schedule are hidden and I see `Your inputs have changed. Select Calculate to see updated results.`

116	- **AC-4.3** Given the message from AC-4.1 is showing, when I Calculate with valid inputs, then results for the new inputs are shown and the message disappears.
117	- **AC-4.4** Given results are showing, when I change the currency or the theme, then the results stay visible (these settings do not change the calculation).

119	## S-5 Use it comfortably on a phone
120	**Role:** R-1 Prospective Borrower · **Serves:** J-11 · **Scope:** v1 · **Status:** Not implemented
121	
122	"As a Prospective Borrower, I want the calculator to work well on my phone, so that I can check an offer wherever I am."
123	
124	- **AC-5.1** Given a viewport 360 px wide, when the page loads and after I calculate L-MAX (480 schedule rows), then the page never scrolls horizontally (document width ≤ viewport width).
125	- **AC-5.2** Given a viewport 360 px wide, then every input, select and button is at least 44 × 44 CSS px and fully visible without zooming.
126	- **AC-5.3** Given a viewport 360 px wide and L-A results, when I scroll the schedule, then the schedule scrolls inside its own area and its column headers stay visible while scrolling.
127	- **AC-5.4** Given any device, then **Loan amount** and **Annual interest rate** have `inputmode="decimal"` and **Loan tenure** has `inputmode="numeric"`, so that phones show a number keypad.
128	- **AC-5.5** Given a viewport 1280 px wide, then the form and the results sit side by side; given a viewport 768 px wide or narrower, they are stacked with the form above the results.
129	- **AC-5.6** Given a viewport 360 px wide and L-MAX results, then every amount in the summary is fully visible (wrapping onto a new line is allowed; clipping is not).

131	## S-6 Choose a light or dark display
132	**Role:** R-1 Prospective Borrower · **Serves:** J-10 · **Scope:** v1 · **Status:** Not implemented
133	
134	"As a Prospective Borrower, I want the app to match a light or dark display, so that I can read figures comfortably at any time of day."
135	
136	- **AC-6.1** Given no saved theme preference, when the page loads on a device set to dark mode, then the app uses the dark theme; on a device set to light mode, it uses the light theme.
137	- **AC-6.2** Given the **Theme** control offers `System`, `Light` and `Dark`, when I choose `Dark` on a device set to light mode, then the app switches to the dark theme immediately (and likewise for `Light`).
138	- **AC-6.3** Given I chose `Dark`, when I reload the page, then the dark theme is still used and `Dark` is still selected.
139	- **AC-6.4** Given `System` is selected, when the device switches between light and dark mode while the page is open, then the app follows without a reload.
140	- **AC-6.5** Given either theme, then body text and error text have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against their background. *(Checked against the theme colour tokens.)*
141	- **AC-6.6** Given the browser blocks storage, when I change the theme, then it changes for the current visit and no error is shown.

143	## S-7 Choose the currency amounts are shown in
144	**Role:** R-1 Prospective Borrower · **Serves:** J-3 · **Scope:** v1 · **Status:** Not implemented
145	
146	"As a Prospective Borrower, I want to see amounts in Pakistani rupees or US dollars, so that the figures read like the quote I was given."
147	
148	- **AC-7.1** Given a first visit, when the page loads, then **Currency** is `PKR (Rs)`, the loan amount label reads `Loan amount (Rs)`, and results for L-A show `Rs 88,848.79`.
149	- **AC-7.2** Given L-A results in PKR, when I select `USD ($)`, then every amount in the summary shows the `$` symbol (e.g. `$88,848.79`), the schedule headers show `($)`, the loan amount label reads `Loan amount ($)`, the numbers themselves are unchanged (no conversion), and the results stay visible.
150	- **AC-7.3** Given I selected `USD ($)`, when I reload the page, then `USD ($)` is still selected.
151	- **AC-7.4** Given the currency control is visible, then the note `Changing currency changes the symbol only. Amounts are not converted.` is shown next to it.
152	- **AC-7.5** Given a saved calculation made in PKR, when I switch to USD, then that saved entry still shows its amounts in `Rs`.

154	## S-8 Work entirely from the keyboard
155	**Role:** R-2 Loan Advisor · **Serves:** J-4 · **Scope:** v1 · **Status:** Not implemented
156	
157	"As a Loan Advisor, I want to do everything from the keyboard, so that I can produce quotes quickly without reaching for the mouse."
158	
159	- **AC-8.1** Given the page has loaded, when I press Tab repeatedly, then focus moves in this order: **Theme** → **Currency** → **Loan amount** → **Annual interest rate** → **Loan tenure** → **Tenure unit** → **Calculate** → **Reset** → the schedule area (only when results are shown) → for each saved calculation, its **Restore** then its **Delete** → **Clear all** (only when enabled). Shift+Tab moves in reverse.
160	- **AC-8.2** Given valid L-A values, when I press Enter while focus is in **Loan amount**, **Annual interest rate** or **Loan tenure**, then the app calculates exactly as if I had selected **Calculate**.

166	## S-9 Start a fresh quote in one step
167	**Role:** R-2 Loan Advisor · **Serves:** J-4 · **Scope:** v1 · **Status:** Not implemented
168	
169	"As a Loan Advisor, I want to clear the form in one step, so that I can start the next quote immediately."
170	
171	- **AC-9.1** Given inputs, results and/or error messages are showing, when I select **Reset**, then all three inputs are empty, the unit returns to **Years**, results, schedule, stale-results message and error messages are removed, and focus moves to **Loan amount**.
172	- **AC-9.2** Given currency `USD ($)`, theme `Dark` and two saved calculations, when I select **Reset**, then currency, theme and saved calculations are unchanged.
173	- **AC-9.3** Given an already empty form, when I select **Reset**, then the form stays empty and no error is shown.

175	## S-10 See how each payment splits into interest and principal
176	**Role:** R-2 Loan Advisor · **Serves:** J-5 · **Scope:** v1 · **Status:** Not implemented
177	
178	"As a Loan Advisor, I want a month-by-month schedule showing interest and principal in each payment, so that I can explain exactly how the quote was reached."
179	
180	- **AC-10.1** Given L-A, when I Calculate, then a **Repayment schedule** table with 12 rows and the columns **Month**, **Payment (Rs)**, **Interest (Rs)**, **Principal (Rs)**, **Balance (Rs)** is shown.

The opening balance is the loan amount for row 1 and the previous row's Balance after that. *(Property test.)*

190	**Role:** R-2 Loan Advisor · **Serves:** J-6 · **Scope:** v1 · **Status:** Not implemented
191	
192	"As a Loan Advisor, I want my recent calculations kept on this device, so that I can bring back an earlier quote exactly without retyping it."
193	
194	Saved calculations are stored only in this browser on this device. They are never sent anywhere.

46	### D-01 Three roles
47	- **Proposal:** R-1 Prospective Borrower (decides whether to borrow), R-2 Loan Advisor (quotes customers professionally: speed, precision, recall, privacy), R-3 Existing Borrower (tracks a loan already running).
48	- **Why:** Their needs differ, and those differences explain why history, delete, keyboard speed and the schedule exist. One "user" role could not justify those stories.
49	- **Alternative:** Two roles (drop R-3). This saves no build work, because the schedule is needed anyway, but it weakens the product story.
50	
51	### D-02 Input bounds
52	- **Proposal:** Loan amount 1,000 to 1,000,000,000 (up to 2 dp); rate 0 to 50% (up to 2 dp); tenure 1 to 40 years or 1 to 480 months (whole numbers).
53	- **Why:** These cover consumer, car and home loans in Pakistan and the US with headroom (PKR property loans run into the hundreds of millions; Pakistan's policy rate peaked at 22% in 2023). The upper limits stop absurd inputs, and the calculation has been proven correct across the whole range (D-03).
54	- **Alternative:** Tighter limits, such as 30 years and 36%. These are simpler to explain but reject some edge-case real loans.
55	
56	### D-03 Schedule rounding method
57	- **Proposal:** Re-compute the instalment from the remaining balance each month, rounding to 2 dp (tech spec §5.2). The headline monthly payment is the standard EMI. Individual months may differ by at most 0.01, and the app says so when they do.
58	- **Why:** The usual "fixed instalment, last one adjusts" method breaks within normal ranges. For example, Rs 10,000 at 36% over 359 months pays off 7 months early, and Rs 10,000.82 at 30% over 360 months gives a final instalment of 1,767.73 against a regular 250.05. The brief says "never a wrong result". Our method was verified exactly across about 1,700 cases, including every boundary corner.
59	- **Trade-off:** Payments alternate by a paisa or cent (for example 88,848.79 and 88,848.78). This is honest and disclosed.
60	- **Alternatives:** (a) The fixed-instalment method with much tighter bounds (still fails for small loans at long tenures). (b) Show unrounded values (rows wouldn't add up to the cent).
61	
62	### D-04 Explicit Calculate; results hidden when inputs change
63	- **Proposal:** Calculate on button press or Enter, not live while typing. Editing any input hides the old results and shows a "inputs have changed" message.
64	- **Why:** Live calculation flashes errors mid-typing (for example "1" is below the minimum while typing "1000"). Hiding stale results enforces R-1's "must never see results that don't match the inputs".
65	- **Alternative:** Live calculation with debounced validation. It feels slicker but needs more edge-case rules.
66	
67	### D-05 Currency
68	- **Proposal:** Default PKR. Options PKR (`Rs 1,234.56`) and USD (`$1,234.56`). Always 2 decimals, standard 3-digit grouping. The symbol only changes; amounts are never converted (a note says so). History entries keep their own currency, and Restore switches to it.
69	- **Why:** The target users are Pakistan-first. Conversion would need live exchange rates (a network service, which the brief rules out for running locally).
70	- **Open sub-question:** Pakistani banks usually quote whole rupees. We keep 2 dp for consistency with ISO 4217 (PKR has 2 minor units). Change to 0 dp for PKR?
71	- **Decision (owner, 2026-10-17):** Approved as proposed. PKR keeps **2 dp**; the sub-question is closed. All reference values stay as they are.

74	- **Proposal:** Switching Years ↔ Months keeps the typed number (5 years becomes 5 months) and marks results stale.
75	- **Why:** Converting breaks for non-multiples (18 months = 1.5 years, which is not a whole number). Keeping the number is predictable, and the stale message prevents misreading.

149	## 4. Input parsing and validation
150	
151	Inputs are `<input type="text">`, **not** `type="number"`. `type="number"` behaves differently across browsers: Firefox accepts letters, `value` becomes `""` for invalid text so errors can't be diagnosed, and the mouse wheel changes values. Add `inputmode` per AC-5.4 and `autocomplete="off"`.
152	
153	### 4.1 Normalisation (before validation)
154	
155	| Field | Steps |
156	|---|---|
157	| Loan amount | Trim whitespace, then remove **all** `,` characters (accepts `1,000,000` and lakh-style `10,00,000`). |
158	| Interest rate | Trim, remove **one** trailing `%`, trim again. |
159	| Loan tenure | Trim. |
160	
161	### 4.2 Rules (checked in this order, stopping at the first failure per field)
162	
163	Number pattern: `^-?(\d+(\.\d*)?|\.\d+)$`. It rejects `1e6`, `+5`, `1.2.3`, `abc` and the empty string. "Decimal places" means the count of digits after `.`, so `5.` has 0. **All comparisons use `Decimal`**, never `Number`, so 40-digit inputs compare correctly.
164	
165	| Field | 1. Empty | 2. Format | 3. Precision | 4. Range |
166	|---|---|---|---|---|
167	| Loan amount | `AMOUNT_REQUIRED` | not a number → `AMOUNT_NAN` | more than 2 dp → `AMOUNT_DECIMALS` | outside 1,000 to 1,000,000,000 inclusive → `AMOUNT_RANGE` |
168	| Interest rate | `RATE_REQUIRED` | → `RATE_NAN` | more than 2 dp → `RATE_DECIMALS` | outside 0 to 50 inclusive → `RATE_RANGE` |
169	| Loan tenure | `TENURE_REQUIRED` | not `^-?\d+$` → `TENURE_WHOLE` (also covers `abc` and `2.5`) | n/a | Years: outside 1 to 40 → `TENURE_RANGE_YEARS`; Months: outside 1 to 480 → `TENURE_RANGE_MONTHS` |
170	
171	A negative number passes the format check and fails on range, so `-500` gets the range message (AC-2.4).

175	- `P` = loan amount as `Decimal`
176	- `n` = tenure × 12 when the unit is years, otherwise the tenure (an integer from 1 to 480)
177	- `annualRate` = `Decimal`
178	- `r = annualRate / 1200` (monthly rate as a fraction, kept exact)

180	## 5. Calculation algorithm (normative)
181	
182	Configure `Decimal.set({ precision: 40, rounding: Decimal.ROUND_HALF_UP })`. `round2(x)` = `x.toDecimalPlaces(2, Decimal.ROUND_HALF_UP)`.
183	
184	### 5.1 EMI function
185	
186	```
187	EMI(B, r, m) = B / m                                if r = 0
188	             = B × r × (1 + r)^m / ((1 + r)^m − 1)  otherwise
189	```
190	
191	### 5.2 Schedule (re-amortising, cent-accurate)
192	
193	```
194	balance ← P
195	for k = 1 … n:
196	    interest_k ← round2(balance × r)
197	    if k < n:
198	        payment_k   ← round2(EMI(balance, r, n − k + 1))
199	        principal_k ← payment_k − interest_k
200	    else:
201	        principal_k ← balance
202	        payment_k   ← principal_k + interest_k
203	    balance ← balance − principal_k
204	    row_k ← { month: k, payment_k, interest_k, principal_k, balance }
205	```
206	
207	Outputs:
208	- **Monthly payment** (headline) = `payment_1` (the standard EMI rounded to 2 dp)
209	- **Total interest** = Σ interest_k
210	- **Total amount payable** = Σ payment_k
211	- **Rounding note shown** = true if any payment_k ≠ payment_1
212	
213	### 5.3 Why this method (do not "simplify" it)
214	
215	The common textbook method fixes the payment at `round2(EMI)` for every month and lets the last month absorb the difference. But the half-cent rounding error compounds at the loan rate. Within our accepted input range this produces wrong-looking results, for example:
216	- Rs 10,000 at 36% for 359 months: the loan is paid off **7 months early** (month 352).
217	- Rs 10,000.82 at 30% for 360 months: the fixed instalment is 250.05 but the final instalment is **1,767.73**.
218	
219	Re-computing the instalment from the remaining balance each month stops the error compounding. We verified over the whole input range (exact decimal simulation, about 1,700 cases including every boundary corner) that it ends at exactly 0.00, never ends early, never produces a negative principal, and that **every payment is within 0.01 of the headline payment**. Every row stays verifiable by hand: interest = opening balance × r, rounded, and principal = payment − interest.
220	
221	### 5.4 Invariants (property-tested with fast-check over the full valid input domain)
222	
223	For every valid (P, rate, n):
224	1. Number of rows = n.
225	2. For every row: `payment = interest + principal` exactly.
226	3. For every row: `interest = round2(opening × r)`, where opening is P for row 1 and the previous row's balance after that.
227	4. For every row: `0 ≤ principal ≤ opening` and `balance ≥ 0`.
228	5. Final balance = 0.00 exactly. Σ principal = P exactly.
229	6. For every row: `|payment − payment_1| ≤ 0.01`.
230	7. Total amount payable = P + total interest, exactly.
231	8. Results are identical when the same tenure is entered as years or as the equivalent number of months.
232	
233	If a property test finds a counterexample: **stop, record it, and report it to the human.** Do not change the algorithm or loosen an invariant without approval.

350	## 9. Persistence
351	
352	### 9.1 Safe storage
353	
354	`safeStorage` checks availability once at start-up (set and remove a probe key inside try/catch). Every read and write is wrapped. Failures return `{ ok: false }` and are never thrown to the UI. If storage is unavailable: settings work in memory for the visit (AC-6.6), and history shows `history.unavailable` (AC-11.9).
355	
356	### 9.2 Keys and schemas (version 1)
357	
358	- `emi-calc.v1.settings` → `{ "currency": "PKR" | "USD", "theme": "system" | "light" | "dark" }`. Defaults: `PKR`, `system`.
359	- `emi-calc.v1.history` → array (newest first, at most 20) of:
360	
361	```json
362	{
363	  "id": "string (crypto.randomUUID, or a timestamp-plus-counter fallback)",
364	  "createdAt": "ISO-8601 string",
365	  "currency": "PKR",
366	  "input": { "amount": "1000000", "rate": "12", "tenure": 1, "unit": "years" },
367	  "monthlyPayment": "88848.79"
368	}
369	```
370	
371	Only these fields are stored, never the schedule. **If the value is not valid JSON or not an array, treat the history as empty.** On load, an element is kept only if **all** of these hold, and otherwise it is dropped (D-14):
372	1. A type guard passes: string `id`; `createdAt` with `!isNaN(Date.parse(createdAt))`; `currency` is `PKR` or `USD`; `input.amount` and `input.rate` are strings; `Number.isInteger(input.tenure)`; `input.unit` is `years` or `months`; string `monthlyPayment`.
373	2. `validateInputs({ ...input, tenure: String(input.tenure) })` returns `ok`.
374	3. `toCanonical(value)` deep-equals the stored `input`, so only canonical entries are restored.
375	4. The stored `monthlyPayment` equals `round2(emi(P, r, n))` as a `Decimal`. Use `emi`, not a full schedule, so loading 20 entries stays cheap.
376	
377	After that, later duplicates of an `id` are dropped and the list is truncated to 20. History line 2 (`{monthly} per month`) shows the recomputed value. Nothing throws (AC-11.10).

379	### 9.3 Saving rules
380	
381	- Save only after a successful calculation.
382	- Skip the save if the newest entry has the same canonical `input` **and** `currency` (AC-11.5).
383	- Insert at index 0 and truncate to 20 (AC-11.6).
384	- If the write fails (for example, quota exceeded), switch to the unavailable state for the rest of the visit.
385	- **Clear all** removes the key entirely (AC-12.4).
386	- **Two tabs (D-13):** every save, delete and clear-all **re-reads storage first** and then writes, so stale in-memory state is never written back. The duplicate check compares against the newest entry as just re-read. Delete works by `id`, never by index.
387	- Listen for the `storage` event on the history key and reload the list. `newValue === null` means the list is now empty. If the entry that had focus is removed this way, focus moves to the **Saved calculations** heading.
